title: Soviet/Warsaw Pact PG-7V (RPG-7) 6-round wooden ammunition crate — ящик укупорочный для выстрелов ПГ-7В
era: 1961–1980s Soviet/Warsaw Pact pattern (PG-7V adopted 1961 with RPG-7); pattern unchanged through late Cold War, photographed example is Bulgarian export production with English export stencils

sources.arcon_pg7v: Arcon Partners Ltd (licensed Bulgarian arms exporter), PG-7V round datasheet, PACKING section — verbatim: 'Rounds in a wooden case for transportation: 6 grenades and 6 start boosters, packed separately … Wooden case dimensions: Overall, (mm): 798 x 452 x 245. Gross weight, (kg): 33. Case volume, (m3): 0.088. Class of explosion hazard: UN 0292, 1.1F' — https://arconpartners.net/products/ammunition/grenade-launchers/40-mm-pg-7v-round-with-high-explosive-anti-tank-grenade-pg-7-heat-for-40-mm-hand-grenade-launcher-rpg-7v/
sources.arcon_pg7vm: Arcon Partners Ltd, PG-7VM round datasheet, PACKING: wooden case 899 x 498 x 294 mm, 39 kg gross, 0.128 m3, 6 rounds — https://arconpartners.net/products/ammunition/grenade-launchers/40-mm-pg-7vm-round-with-high-explosive-anti-tank-grenade-pg-7m-heat-for-40-mm-hand-grenade-launcher-rpg-7v/
sources.arcon_og7v: Arcon Partners Ltd, OG-7V round datasheet, PACKING: wooden case 830 x 430 x 275 mm, 50 kg gross, 0.100 m3, 18 rounds — https://arconpartners.net/products/ammunition/grenade-launchers/40-mm-og-7v-round-with-high-explosive-fragmentation-grenade-og-7-for-40-mm-hand-grenade-launcher-rpg-7v/
sources.militarysklad_listing: MILITARY RANGE (militarysklad.cz) Czech surplus listing 'Bedna dřevěná od munice PG 7, použitá': approx 80 x 40 x 22 cm, 16 kg empty, wooden crate with lid, two metal folding carry handles, lid hinged on two metal hinges, two front latches (přezky) — https://www.militarysklad.cz/detail/bedna-drevena-od-munice-pg-7-pouzita-1000086506
sources.militarysklad_photo_closed: Product photo 1 (closed crate, 3/4 view) — olive-green crate, 2 lid battens with steel end-straps, 2 front flip-latches, end bail handle, black stencils 'PG-7VM Practice-T / 01-⑪-16 / Gross wt 32 kg / 6pcs / 87dm³ / HEAD END / T / -40C +50C', UN 1.4S diamond label — https://www.militarysklad.cz/Content/custom/img_products/87027129.jpg
sources.militarysklad_photo_open: Product photo 2 (open crate) — raw unpainted pine interior and lid underside (3 lid planks), paper packing list glued under lid, scalloped transverse cradle dividers for 6 rounds, square vertical corner/intermediate posts, rear strap hinge visible — https://www.militarysklad.cz/Content/custom/img_products/87027129-1.jpg
sources.militarysklad_photo_end: Product photo 3 (end face) — folding steel wire bail handle on riveted plate, riveted steel corner angle straps on both vertical corners, chamfered lid-batten ends with screwed steel straps, end stencil 'PG-7M / 01-⑪-16 / Practice' — https://www.militarysklad.cz/Content/custom/img_products/87027129-2.jpg
sources.inertproducts_replica: Inert Products LLC replica PG-7V crate (copied from original): 32.13 x 18.03 x 9.84 in = 816 x 458 x 250 mm — https://inertproducts.com/product/pg-7-rockets-in-crate-replica-weapon-cache-crate/
sources.studfile_okraska: Russian artillery textbook §4.4 'Окраска и маркировка боеприпасов' — verbatim: '…зеленого цвета на деревянную укупорку боеприпасов'; 'На укупорочных ящиках с выстрелами, снарядами и боевыми зарядами на боковой и торцевой стенках наносят маркировку, характеризующую содержимое. Кроме обычных сведений указываются количество штук и масса брутто.' — https://studfile.net/preview/5082433/page:19/
sources.ruwiki_marking: Wikipedia (ru) «Маркировка боеприпасов», crate marking: lid carries масса брутто + transport danger sign (digit '2' in triangle, apex toward the hinge side); side wall carries designation, lot, year, factory code, quantity — https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Маркировка_боеприпасов
sources.weaponland_marking: weaponland.ru «Маркировка инженерных боеприпасов Советской Армии» — 'Ящики… обычно окрашены в темно-зеленый цвет, реже некрашеные.'; black stencil layout: designation + quantity, factory–batch–year with dashes, explosive type, gross weight; warning stencils; danger triangle — https://weaponland.ru/publ/markirovka_inzhenernykh_boepripasov_sovetskoj_armii/20-1-0-577
sources.livinghistory_ukuporka: livinghistory.ru reenactor thread 'Изготовление деревянной укупорки и ящиков' — measured original WW2 45mm crate: 520x380x200, board thickness 20 mm, lid/bottom batten (рейка) 50x25 mm; ZIS-3 76mm crate 785x510x160 per 1949 manual; ГОСТ/ОСТ dovetail → wartime nailed butt joints; turn-latch sealed with wire — http://livinghistory.ru/topic/62192-izgotovlenie-dereviannoi-ukuporki-i-iaschikov/
sources.ge_catalogue: General Equipment RPG-7V2 product catalogue PDF — new-production RPG-7 launcher crate (raw wood photo): 1200 x 440 x 331 mm, 4 launchers, 60 kg — https://www.generalequipment.info/RPG-7V2%20Product%20Catalogue.pdf
sources.user_ref_photos: User-supplied reference photos: (1) opened olive crate, raw pine plank interior, internal corner blocks, riveted steel flip-latches, steel strap hinges, black Cyrillic stencils «125-Д81 …» (= 125mm Д-81 tank-gun crate, larger alternate type); (2) closed grey-green crate with two lid battens, front flip-latches, steel side carry handle, dense stencils (= matches the PG-7 family pattern)

box_dimensions.src: arcon_pg7v (manufacturer datasheet); cross-corroborated: photographed crate's own '87dm³ / Gross wt 32 kg' stencil vs computed 798×452×245 = 88.4 dm³ (militarysklad_photo_closed); replica 816×458×250 (inertproducts_replica); Czech surplus rough 80×40×22 cm, 16 kg empty (militarysklad_listing)
box_dimensions.note: Primary type = PG-7V (RPG-7) 6-round crate, standard two-man-carry укупорка. Family variants: PG-7VM 899×498×294, OG-7V 830×430×275. Gross 33 kg / 16 kg empty.

construction.body_walls: Long walls of 2 horizontal planks (visible seam on front face); butt-jointed and nailed, riveted steel corner angle straps on the end-face vertical corners; 2 proud vertical wooden cleats on the front face between latch positions
construction.board_thickness_note: ANALOG value measured on an original WW2 45mm crate (livinghistory_ukuporka), not on a PG-7 crate; photo proportions consistent
construction.corner_joinery: Postwar: nailed butt joints + internal vertical corner posts + external riveted steel corner angles
construction.interior: RAW unpainted pine throughout: corner + intermediate posts, longitudinal rails, scalloped transverse cradles for 6 rounds; paper packing list glued to lid underside

hardware.latches: 2 riveted steel flip-latches (hasp-and-toggle) on the long front face at the lid seam, in line with internal post positions; Soviet turn-latches carry sealing-wire holes + lead seal
hardware.hinges: 2 steel strap hinges at the rear long face; Soviet convention: danger-triangle apex on lid points toward the hinges
hardware.handles: 2 folding steel wire bail handles, one centered on each END face, mounted on riveted steel plates — two-man carry; NO rope handles on this type
hardware.corner_hardware: Riveted steel angle straps wrapping both vertical corners of each end face; short steel straps screwed over the chamfered lid-batten ends
hardware.src: militarysklad_listing, militarysklad_photo_closed, militarysklad_photo_end, militarysklad_photo_open, livinghistory_ukuporka, ruwiki_marking

paint_markings.exterior_color: Protective green / olive-drab (studfile_okraska; weaponland_marking; photographed crate is worn olive-khaki)
paint_markings.interior: Raw unpainted pine — exterior painted only
paint_markings.stencil_color: Black paint on the green ground
paint_markings.stencil_content_layout: Front long wall: round index («ПГ-7В»), lot–factory–year group, «БРУТТО … КГ», piece count «6 ШТ», volume dm³, temperature ovals; end wall: index + lot group + nature; lid (convention): масса брутто + danger triangle '2' apex toward hinges (photographed export lid unstencilled)
paint_markings.star: NO star on this crate type — none present in any photo of the pattern; do not add one

lid.planks: 3 longitudinal planks (lid underside visible in open photo)
lid.battens: 2 transverse battens on top, one near each end, ends chamfered ~45°, secured by screwed steel straps
lid.batten_section_mm: 50 x 25 (ANALOG: measured WW2 45mm crate lid рейка — livinghistory_ukuporka; photo proportions consistent)

derivation.volume_check: 798 × 452 × 245 mm = 0.0884 m³ — matches manufacturer 0.088 m³ and the crate's own '87dm³' stencil; src: geometric derivation from arcon_pg7v + militarysklad_photo_closed
derivation.wall_plank_width_mm: ≈100 each: body side ≈ 245 − 20 (lid) − 25 (batten) ≈ 200 mm over 2 visible planks; src: geometric derivation from arcon_pg7v envelope + plank count + 20 mm analog thickness
derivation.lid_plank_width_mm: ≈150 each: 452 mm over 3 lid planks; src: geometric derivation from arcon_pg7v + militarysklad_photo_open
derivation.body_lid_split_mm: lid board 20 + battens 25 proud; body 0→225, seam at 225; src: geometric derivation from box_dimensions + lid.thickness + battens
derivation.hardware_sizes_mm: flip-latch plate ≈ 60×90, strap hinge ≈ 50×100, bail handle ≈ 150 wide × 60 reach, corner angle strap ≈ 30 wide × 200 tall, front cleat ≈ 40 wide × 200 tall × 15 proud — scaled from militarysklad photos against the 798/452/245 envelope; src: geometric derivation from box_dimensions + militarysklad_photo_closed/_end
derivation.empty_vs_gross_weight: 33 kg gross − 16 kg empty ≈ 17 kg contents — consistent, mutually corroborating
